author: Declan Walsh
title: Connecticut lottery players used Powerball prize for big win as jackpot grows to $1.4 billion - NewsBreak
text:
By Declan Walsh ,
2 hours ago A customer holds Powerball lottery tickets for a $750 Million grand prize jackpot inside the Bluebird Liquor Store, which has sold winning tickets in past large lottery jackpots, in Hawthorne, California on Aug. 25, 2025. (PATRICK T. FALLON/AFP via Getty Images) A Berlin couple transformed a modest return from a Powerball ticket into a life-changing windfall, investing the winnings into a Fortune scratch game ticket from the CT Lottery.
The ticket, purchased at the South Windsor Pride Convenience Store on John Fitch Boulevard, turned out to be a $500,000 winner, according to a CT Lottery press release. The couple quickly brought the ticket to the CT Lottery Claims Center in Wallingford, still in a state of disbelief after their half-million dollar prize was confirmed.
“I was originally buying some Powerball tickets with buddies, won a few bucks and then bought some scratch games,” said the husband, who was not identified, in the CT Lottery press release. “After we won, I called my wife and we both raced over to the CLC claims center to verify the ticket.”
That Sept. 1 drawing produced a pair of additional Connecticut winners, with a New Haven man earning $50,000 that he plans to spend on house repairs, lottery officials said. Additionally, a Powerball ticket worth $150,000 was purchased in Winsted at the Stop & Shop on New Hartford Road. The ticket has not been claimed yet.
The next drawing is scheduled for Wednesday evening at 10:59 p.m., for which the jackpot has climbed to an estimated $1.4 billion, with an estimated cash value of $634 million. Should a winner be selected, it would be the fourth-largest Powerball prize in game history.
Overall odds of Powerball are 1 in 24.9, while odds of winning the jackpot are 1 in 292.2 million, according to the CT Lottery. Players must be 18 or older to purchase lottery tickets.
